learning: If line_loss_events fall toward 0.5 or below on the s-bend and slalom, turn authority was the limit; next tune wheel_track against it. If line loss stays at 1.0 per run, the next test should look at a fixed point on the course where all sensors lose the line (for example the start), not at more geometry changes.
notes: Single-change test: wheel_radius 0.03 to 0.035 m on the iteration 3 package. Controller and sensing are unchanged, so the race isolates turn authority and ground speed. The package is complete and runnable against the contract limits.
rationale: Iteration 3 (mass 0.6 kg, sensors at y 0.03 m, +/-3 cm span, 16 mm sensors) scored 46.16 and still lost the line once per run on all three tracks (oval 1.0, s-bend 1.0, slalom 1.0). Max_error reached 0.061 to 0.064 m, which is the 0.06 m off-track limit. Steering oscillation stayed low at 0.07 to 0.13, so the failure is line loss on bends, not jitter. Sensor span (iteration 1), sensor offset (iteration 2) and mass (iteration 3) have each left line loss at about 1.0 per run, so the geometry's sensing and inertia are not the limit. The Builder's test is wheel_radius 0.03 to 0.035 m, with everything else held at iteration 3. A larger radius gives more yaw rate per unit wheel-speed difference and more ground speed, which tests turn authority directly. I keep the controller identical to iteration 3 (kp 2.5, ki 0, kd 0.2, base_speed 1.5, last_direction recovery, weights scaled to x) so any change in line loss can be attributed to the wheel radius alone. base_speed 1.5 still gives a PWM base well within limits at the higher ground speed. Expected, not measured: fewer line-loss events on the s-bend and slalom, and completion_time falling toward 3 s.
